subject: Throughput & latency gating + GPU fitment — validation asks and pilot plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@helixhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Throughput & latency gating + GPU fitment — validation asks and pilot plan

Hi Emma / Helix team —

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope a dedicated-capacity pilot that validates your SLOs. Short version: we understand your product requirements but need a small benchmark/data handoff to size reserved capacity and choose the right GPU profile.

Helix SLOs we heard on the call (please correct if off):
- Streaming text generation p95 latency <= 150 ms for 512-token responses
- Sustained throughput: 300 requests/sec (avg payload ~220 tokens)
- Peak concurrency: 200 concurrent sessions (short bursts to 400 for 30s)
- Availability target: 99.9% during business hours; lower tier outside BH

Concrete asks from Redwood to scope pilot:
1) Attach: a small sample of typical requests (we discussed ~1k sample payloads) — filename: sample_payloads.jsonl.
2) Your current tokenization distribution (we only need rough percentiles) or a short CSV of request sizes.
3) Any transformations you do client-side (e.g., n-of-k prompts, reranking) that affect total token count per request.

Proposed pilot plan (3-week technical pilot):
- Week 0: Data handoff + mutual action plan (MAP) sign-off
- Week 1: Benchmark runs on 2 GPU profiles (A100 80GB single-node baseline, H100 80GB candidate) with your sample workload (including streaming enabled)
- Week 2: Stress test for concurrency/peak bursts and validate KV cache effectiveness; final report + recommendation

Preliminary reserved capacity suggestion (for pilot only):
- Start with a 2-node H100 pool OR 3x A100 80GB nodes depending on quantization and batchability. Ben will outline the cost/perf matrix in a follow-up.

Deliverables from Redwood:
- CSV of measured p50/p95/p99 latency for streaming and non-streaming paths
- Throughput curves vs batch size and concurrency
- Recommended reserved throughput with guardrails and autoscale thresholds

Can you confirm the sample payload delivery by Friday (May 22) and whether Helix prefers we test H100 first or A100 first? If you want, we can also add an L4/RTX-based low-cost path but that will have higher latency for streaming.

Thanks — will keep this short and iterate once we have the samples.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: helix_slo_matrix.xlsx (referenced)

From: Emma Liu <emma@helixhealth.ai>

Cc: ops@helixhealth.ai
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Throughput & latency gating + GPU fitment — validation asks and pilot plan

Thanks Karthik — 

This aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications and I attached two files: helix_slo_matrix.xlsx and sample_payloads.jsonl.
- The p95 target is for in-session streaming responses to the main user prompt (post-filter). If a rerank occurs it adds an extra call — we included that in the payloads.
- Typical token breakdown: median 180 tokens, 75th 320, 95th 620. The 512 number is our most common response cap but we do have longer tails.
- For quantization: we are open to 4-bit if quality checks pass, but procurement will prefer A100 family unless H100 shows a clear latency advantage.

We can deliver the sample payloads and the spreadsheet is attached. We can do H100-first if Redwood thinks that gives us a better chance of hitting 150ms p95 for the 512/620 token buckets.

Next step for us: I’ll confirm by EOD that ops can share a test account and the anonymized traffic patterns. Happy to do MAP sign-off once we have the benchmark criteria added.

—
Emma Liu
Head of Platform Engineering | HelixHealth
emma@helixhealth.ai

Attachments: helix_slo_matrix.xlsx, sample_payloads.jsonl

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 15:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Throughput & latency gating + GPU fitment — validation asks and pilot plan

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Emma — got both attachments and the token percentiles; that helps a lot.

Ben / Soojin — tagging you on the workload distribution and initial asks so you can propose the detailed test matrix. Key constraints: streaming p95 <=150ms on the 75th/95th buckets is non-negotiable for Helix. They also need sustained 300 qps with 200 concurrent sessions.

I propose we include the following in the Redwood benchmark harness:
- Streaming path (chunked token-by-token) with early-termination handling to replicate UX
- KV cache enabled for repeated prefixes (we saw Helix will have ~30% repeated context)
- Quantization runs: FP16 baseline, 4-bit quantized candidate
- Test matrix axes: GPU type (A100/H100), batch sizes (1, 2, 4, 8), concurrency levels (50, 150, 300), token lengths (median/75/95 bins)

Can Ben post the tentative reserved-capacity pilots numbers (nodes/estimated reserved throughput) and a rough cost delta? Also Soojin — please note we should include streaming tail latency (p99) in the report since UX is sensitive.

I’ll assemble a MAP draft with the acceptance criteria and share the Drive link shortly. Emma — if procurement needs a preliminary cost estimate to start internal approvals, let me know and I’ll include a “pilot estimate” based on Ben’s numbers.

Thanks,
—
Karthik

Quick internal + external note on sizing and cost tradeoffs. Sending recommendations so Helix can prep procurement expectations.

Baseline assumptions (from sample_payloads + token percentiles):
- Effective avg tokens/request (including reranks & system prompts): ~240 tokens
- Streaming chunk size: 64 tokens per websocket chunk (configurable)
- 30% repeat prefixes usable for KV caching

Pilot configurations (suggested):
A) Cost-optimized baseline: 3x NVIDIA A100 80GB nodes (FP16)
- Estimated sustained qps per node (streaming, p95 target hit for median/75): ~110 qps
- Pilot reserved throughput: 330 qps
- Estimated pilot monthly run cost (on Redwood Dedicated pilot terms): ~USD 11,000 (engineering bench-hours excluded)

B) Performance-first baseline: 2x NVIDIA H100 80GB nodes (mixed precision / optimized kernels)
- Estimated sustained qps per node (streaming, better tail latency): ~180 qps
- Pilot reserved throughput: 360 qps
- Estimated pilot monthly run cost: ~USD 19,000

C) Low-cost cloud GPU (if Helix wants a less expensive fallback): 4x L4/RTX-style nodes — expect higher latency and larger variance; not recommended for hard p95 target.

Notes on quantization: 4-bit runs can reduce memory pressure and increase batch capacity but require model-quality validation; if Helix accepts minor quality delta we can push more effective qps per node.

Recommended pilot: start H100-first for the benchmark (given Helix preference), run FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants. If H100 shows clear p95 improvements for 512+ tokens we recommend an H100 reserved pool; otherwise choose A100 with quantization and larger node count.

Attachments: redwood_gpu_matrix.pdf (includes perf curves and cost delta table)

Action items:
- Redwood (Ben): finalize cost sheet + add estimated time to run full matrix (target: 2 business days for initial runs)
- Helix (Emma): confirm pilot account and MAP sign-off window (EOD Fri)
- Redwood (Soojin): include p99 tail latency and streaming chunk-config sensitivity test in harness

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
